title: Microshift handoff - kernel log & todo
content:
Quick summary:
- Short handoff for the 3am microshift. Spent last 4 hrs debugging a sporadic p99 tail spike on small NVidia box during sustained chat workload. Patch (WIP) reduces one hot-path lock when kv-cache miss/evict happens, but not certain about lock convoy under nvlink saturation.

What I changed (notes):
- Added a fast-path for ephemeral KV eviction check to avoid global mutex in cold-start path (runtime/kv_cache.cc).
- Reduced mutex hold-time around slot allocation: try_lock -> fallback_lock.
- Instrumented counters: kv_evictions_fastpath, kv_evictions_slowpath, kv_lock_wait_us.
- Added short TTL to prefix-cache for chat tests (30s) to simulate churn.

How to reproduce locally (devbox):
1) Start a small repro harness: 
   ./tools/run_microshift.sh --model llama-2-small --clients 25 --seq 1024 --qps 12
2) Tail metrics: prometheus endpoint on :9100/metrics (or run `curl localhost:9100/metrics | grep kv_`)
3) Trigger churn with: `python tools/stress_clients.py --clients 25 --pattern churn`
4) Watch histograms for token latency and kv_lock_wait_us.

Observed behavior this morning: 
- At ~02:45 UTC, p99 jumped by ~180ms for ~3 minutes. During that window: kv_lock_wait_us median increased from ~4us to ~120us; kv_evictions_slowpath rose from 2/min to ~60/min.
- NVLink bandwidth graph (nvidia-smi) shows brief plateauing concurrent with spikes; not conclusive but correlates.
- Heap growth small (10-20MB) so not GC/memory related.

Immediate mitigations tried: 
- Reverted a recent commit that moved prefetching into the caller: made slight improvement but not full.
- Deployed a config: kv_prefix_ttl=30 (was 300) to reduce cold-prefix thrash. Reduced spike duration but frequency unchanged.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Lock convoy on global KV eviction lock when multiple clients cause simultaneous evictions. Slowpath uses vector compaction that's O(n) and holds lock.
2) NVLink saturation slows memory copies (especially during evict+prefetch), increasing time spent in critical section, amplifying convoy.
3) Scheduler co-scheduling on the box (noisy neighbor) caused short-lived CPU stalls leading to lock waitouts.

Quick experiments to try (next shift):
- Replace slowpath compaction with stashing tombstones + lazy compaction triggered by background thread. Cheap to prototype: introduce tombstone vector and background compactor that acquires exclusive lock with backoff.
- Add per-shard eviction locks (shard by prefix hash) to reduce contention; measure on canary.
- Instrument NVLink memcpy durations in runtime (wrap cudaMemcpy with timer) for a short window to validate hypothesis 2.

Commands & snippets I used: 
- Repro harness: `./tools/run_microshift.sh --model llama-2-small --clients 25 --seq 1024 --qps 12`
- Stress pattern: `python tools/stress_clients.py --clients 25 --pattern churn --duration 600`
- Metrics quick check: `curl -s localhost:9100/metrics | egrep 'kv_lock_wait_us|kv_evictions'`
- Heap + cpu: `top -b -n 1` and `nvidia-smi dmon -s u`

Open TODO (short):
- [ ] Draft quick patch for tombstone-based eviction (small prototype) - estimate 1.5-2h.
- [ ] Add NVLink memcpy timer around prefetch path - 30m.
- [ ] Canary per-shard locks behind feature flag - coordinate with infra for canary pool (INF-4821).
- [ ] Run longer churn test (6h) with logging level DEBUG for kv path and collect traces.

Open TODO (handoff items):
- If you take this: prioritize the tombstone prototype first. If p99 still spikes after that, try per-shard locks.
- Leave feature flag off by default; we'll gate canary via rollout console and watch kv_evictions_slowpath metric.
- If you see the p99 spike >200ms for >5 minutes, escalate to SRE (page lists in infra-runbook) and attach the last 10m of prometheus & nvlink logs.

Notes for follow-up tickets: 
- INF-4821: tracked for canary and per-shard lock work (link above).
- INF-4888: request for deeper NVLink profiling and telemetry aggregation (put profiler on cluster nodes for 24h).

Questions for you (next shift):
- Do we have a way to inject artificial NVLink delay locally? (not yet — ask infra)
- Is anyone else experimenting with tombstone compaction? Rashmi, Luca — pinged you in Slack about this prototype.

Other misc observations: 
- I noticed two short-lived kernel WARN logs on 03:12 that mention `kv_slot_alloc` failing a DCHECK in debug builds. Not seen in prod release but worth guarding path.
- There is a small race on slot index wraparound that I will write a unit test for tomorrow.

Handoff status: 
- Current branch `caleb/kv-evict-fastpath` pushed to remote; PR opened (#2291). Patch is partial and guarded behind feature flag `kv_evict_fastpath=true`.
- If you need to revert quickly: `git revert 7f4b8a2` (the two commits that introduced try_lock) and restart service on node.

If you pick this up, LMK in #eng-runtime and drop a short note here with time when you start/stop so I can follow up.

-- Caleb

(quick scratch log end)
